notes: Typed from Griffith's hand copy by Claude Opus 5.5 (pack A), then checked against his Latin letters (the names, titles and formula words of his English rendering, and his notes on the formulae): 1 sign changed by the check. Altar border in four copy rows (fragments). Griffith's raised numbers 2, 3, 6, 8, 11, 12 mark parts of the text; parts 1, 4, 5, 7, 9, 10 are lost, so rows are separated by spaces. Read row 1 to row 4, each right to left. Wavy strokes at the left ends of rows 2-4 and at the right end of row 4 are break lines, not signs. Row 2 starts with an isolated 'i :' right of the wide (wedge-shaped) gap, the end of the lost filiation; the -lowi endings are not rendered by him. Pakharas ends in the se sign (cup with two strokes), consistent with his English s = se. Row 3 is the end of a benediction (A or B): it ends -ẖekete like formula A in Faras 2; his note 'a-ḫrkete in n° 1' (B) cannot be found in this copy, while Faras 2's B reads exactly aḫrkete, so his 'n° 1' there may refer to n° 2. Row 4 is formula C: ḫmlol (his ḫmlêli) : pstḫ (his 'pštḫ in n° 1'). Caveat: the page overviews at 0.3 scale showed the renderings before step 1 was done.

notes: Typed from Griffith's hand copy by Claude Opus 5.5 (pack D), then checked against his Latin letters (the names, titles and formula words of his English rendering, and his notes on the formulae): 26 signs changed by the check. Copy kept against his Latin letters: aroẖteke (his Latin: Arekhatake (a-r-e-ẖ-t-k-e)); itebereke (his Latin: yitebereke); iẖte (formula A) (his Latin: yi- (p. 647: initial yi in n° 21)); dlitwketei(13)telo (his Latin: Zalitawaketiyi in); an : (6)t : mnp (his Latin: prophet of Amanap); ey?[.][.]lo (his Latin: ye. . .); ẖolkte (formula C) (his Latin: ẖêl... (p. 648)). Order follows the raised numbers: rows 1-9 are the border text (parts 1-21), each row read right part, (middle), then left part; row 9 holds the repeated invocation and formulae C (ḫmlol : ẖolkte) and A (ato mẖe : iẖte). Rows 10-12 (parts 22-25) and 13-15 (parts 26-29) are the two field texts on either side of the amphora; Griffith's English reorders the field texts (e.g. 'tereki takabache of the akhararab, in Taketêre' = rows 13-14). 'Bezewi' in his English spells be-ze-wi, matching the copy's bedewi. The '-lo' / '-li' suffixes are omitted in his English. The odd mark after 'Khalalacharêr:' in the print is a blemish. I glimpsed his notes on No. 21 (p. 620: Bezewi, wayekite, shêr, Charimali, yireke, Amenap) while reading No. 20's notes, before reading this copy, so 'first' is not fully blind for those words; I also knew the formula notes on pp. 647-648 from No. 19.
